_note: Hand-written. No generation, no LLM. Every line here was typed by a person and is shipped as reviewed content (SPECS §9). Trait tags in brackets are display-only until traits exist: the rules layer ignores them. Tiles are overworld coordinates, towns are laid out on the map at their real size rather than entered through a transition. Some lines are gated on a named world condition, the rules layer decides what the name means, so no line reads the world directly.
_names_note: Proper nouns the world contains that are neither a person with a sheet nor a place on the map: the burned villages the land grants name, and the river. Declared here because the reject filter on any generated line refuses names that do not exist, and a name that appears only inside a sentence is indistinguishable from an invented one.

facts.muster:pay_fraud: Quartermaster Odile at the Muster signs for soldiers who are dead or never existed, and keeps the difference.
facts.kettle:ford: A ford crosses the Kettle downstream of the bridge, shallow only in dry weeks.
facts.wide_acres:unwatched_stall: There is a market stall in Saltmarch that nobody stands near, the marsh town is off the road and keeps no watch worth the name.
facts.acres:land_grants: The land grants for the Wide Acres, naming each village cleared to make them. One of the names is the one you grew up in.
facts.cairnwell:tiered_law: The working record of how the tiered law is administered: 3 columns, and the third is calculated from the first two.
facts.cinderworks:ledger: The Cinderworks ledger of what the furnaces cost in men, kept in the king's own hand, with the price set against the output.
facts.bank:debts: The bank's book of what the crown owes and to whom. Nearly all of it is owed to one creditor.
facts.muster:signed_orders: The orders to clear the villages, signed. The men who carried them out are named underneath.
facts.cinderworks:death_toll: The Cinderworks has killed 381 men in 11 years, by the ledger Halgrave keeps. Arthur was sent the count every year and kept sending for more stone.
facts.acres:razed_villages: The Wide Acres estates stand on the ground of villages that were cleared to make them. The grants name every one, and Brindle is on the list.
facts.brindle:the_ground: The farmland north of Brindle is Brindle, the same soil, ploughed over. Old Pell worked it before the burning and works it still.
facts.muster:how_the_king_fights: Arthur trained with his own guard and has never changed his opening. He leads with the shield and counters left, and his officers have drilled against it for years.
facts.thornwood:kell: A deserter called Kell is living rough in the Thornwood, east of Harrowgate, by a fire he keeps too small to see from the road.
facts.brindle:that_night: What happened at Brindle: the order was to clear it, the village did not move, and the men who carried it out were told afterwards that it had resisted.
facts.saltmarch:what_leaves: Steel, grain and coin leave the region by sea, on the crown's order and under nobody's seal. Til has the manifests he was told to lose.
facts.law:the_effects: What the tiered law does, case by case: the same offence, three sentences, sorted by what the accused owns and where they were born.
facts.bank:leveraged: The whole industrial project is borrowed, and nearly all of it is owed to one creditor. Arthur's certainty was a bet.
facts.castle:hesper: Nothing goes into Blackcairn without Hesper's mark. She is the door, and she has no deputy.
facts.church:ledgers: The church's own ledgers, which show what Hesper took and from whom. Anselm keeps them because somebody has to.
facts.castle:the_way_in: How a stranger is admitted to Blackcairn: a name on a supply roll, countersigned, and a face that matches it.
facts.king:his_argument: Arthur's case, in his own words: poverty is the enemy, industry is the only thing that has ever ended it, industry needs land, and the villages that would not move were choosing poverty for their grandchildren. He signed the orders himself and will produce them on request.
facts.blackcairn:the_escort: The escort at the gate is not a fixed number. It is whatever the Muster can still spare, and it has been falling for a year.
facts.you:died: You died when Brindle burned, with everybody else.
facts.you:raised: The fairies of the wood brought you back. Your memory is what it cost.
facts.thornwood:axes: Men come into the wood with axes and fire, and the wood is smaller every year.
facts.you:remembered: The fairy knew you before the fire. It is the one witness to your life that is not a piece of paper.
facts.you:owed: The fairy did not choose you because you are someone. She chose you because you are owed something.
facts.thornwood:save_us: The fairies have asked you to save them, if you can.

fairy.name: The fairy
fairy.greeting: You are awake. Do not go yet.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: You died with the others.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: I brought you back. It cost you your memory.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: Men came with axes and fire. The wood is smaller every year.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: We are dying.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: I knew you, before.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: I did not pick someone special. I picked someone who is owed.

options.text: Listen.
options.reply: Find your way in this world. And if you can, save us.

maddox.name: Maddox
maddox.greeting: You walked here. Nobody walks here.

options.text: Who owns this town?
options.reply: Depends who you ask. The Reeve says the king owns it. The king says the Reeve does. Go and ask Tovin, he runs the law here.

options.text: Who applies the law here?
options.reply: Tovin the Reeve. His office is on the square. He will be polite about it and he will still take your money.

options.text: Do soldiers still come through?
options.reply: Fewer every month. They are leaving the army camp up north. Ask Ossa the herbalist, she treats the ones who run.

options.text: Why has bread gone up?
options.reply: Soldiers. The army used to feed them. Now they have left the camp and they buy bread here, and there is no more grain than before.

options.text: Anything I should know?
options.reply: A man drinks here who will not give his name and will not sit with his back to the door. A deserter, I think.

options.text: Is there a man living in the woods?
options.reply: Kell. He has been in the Thornwood two winters. Ossa walks east with a full bag twice a month and comes back with an empty one.

alt_greetings.text: Bread's up again. Third time this month, and nobody can tell me why.

tovin.name: Tovin the Reeve
tovin.greeting: If you want to register, go inside. If you want to complain, go inside. It is the same queue.

options.text: How is the law applied here?
options.reply: By levels. What you pay depends on what you own and on where your father was born. A poor man pays more for the same thing.

options.text: And you think that is fair?
options.reply: No. It is the law and it is not fair. Those are two different things. I have a house and a job and I apply it.

options.text: Does your office cover the army camp?
options.reply: On paper. In practice the camp judges itself, so nobody judges it. Nothing that happens there reaches my desk.

options.text: I want to serve the king.
options.reply: Then I will write you down. You start at the bottom, like everybody. Work will find you.

options.text: I have learned something. I am telling you.
options.reply: I am noting it. It will go up. You only say a thing like that once, so do not say it twice.

alt_greetings.text: If you've come about the grain levy, so has everyone. The answer is the same.

bell.name: Bell
bell.greeting: Careful, the ink is wet. The Reeve counts the pages at the end of the day.

options.text: You know the wealth levels?
options.reply: I copy them every week. 3 columns: what you own, where you come from, what you owe. The third one is worked out from the first two.

options.text: Do you ever copy something slowly?
options.reply: Sometimes. 14 lines an hour instead of 40. It gives a man a week before his sentence is filed.

options.text: Do army papers pass your desk?
options.reply: Only the clean papers. Everything from the camp arrives in order. Tidy paper out of an untidy camp is strange.

ossa.name: Ossa
ossa.greeting: Sit down if you are bleeding. Stand somewhere else if you are not.

reactions.unwelcome: I answer everyone, you as well.
reactions.welcome: Ask, I do not count the questions.

options.text: They say you treat men who have run.
options.reply: I treat anyone who bleeds. I have never asked a soldier for his papers before setting his arm and I will not start today.

options.text: Why are so many of them running?
options.reply: Not the fighting. The pay. There is a quartermaster at the camp, Odile. She signs for soldiers who are dead and keeps their pay.

options.text: Is there one of them you remember?
options.reply: Kell. He lives in the Thornwood, east of here, next to a small fire. Make noise when you get close or he will run.

alt_greetings.text: I saw what you did. Sit if you're bleeding, I said I never ask, and I meant it. But you'll get no more than that from me.

garrick.name: Garrick
garrick.greeting: Mind the wheel. I carry people and goods. I am cheaper than boots.

options.text: Is the bridge the only way over the river?
options.reply: No. There is a ford downstream, half a day away. The water is low in a dry week and nobody watches who crosses there.

options.text: You supply the army camp?
options.reply: I used to. Now they order less and pay me late. Somebody up there is keeping the difference.

options.text: What else travels the road?
options.reply: Soldiers walking away from the camp instead of towards it. And people who listen to what carters say.

wren.name: Wren
wren.greeting: Watch your feet. Half of what is under the ash is worth money. The other half will cut you.

reactions.welcome: You, you do not pay for this.

options.text: You live out here?
options.reply: I work here. Nobody lives in Brindle any more, the village was burned. I came afterwards to collect what was left.

options.text: You must know where nobody is looking.
options.reply: That is the only thing I sell. Go to Saltmarch, on the north side. There is a market stall there with nobody watching it, week after week.

options.text: What do you sell, and to who?
options.reply: Scrap metal. I sell it to the ironworks west of here. 2 copper coins a sack. They never ask where it came from.

halgrave.name: Foreman Halgrave
halgrave.greeting: Careful, the slag stays hot all day. This is the third biggest ironworks in the kingdom.

reactions.welcome: Then you get the whole of it.

alt_greetings.text: Halgrave stands between you and the furnaces and does not move.

options.text: What is it you make here?
options.reply: Iron and steel. Rails, plates, tools, nails. Before the works, 1 child in 4 died here every winter. Now it is 1 in 40.

options.text: How many men has it killed?
options.reply: 381 in 11 years. I write the number down and send it to King Arthur every spring. He reads it and orders the works made bigger.

options.text: You keep a record of the dead?
options.reply: A book with every name and every date. The crown asks for it. I would keep it anyway. If a thing kills 381 men somebody should write it down.

sena.name: Sena
sena.greeting: You are not from the works. Nobody from the works stands looking at it.

alt_greetings.text: Sena watches your hands instead of your face.

options.text: What happened to your hand?
options.reply: Furnace number 4, 6 years ago. The works paid me 11 days of wages and the doctor wrote that it was my own fault.

options.text: How many men has the works killed?
options.reply: Halgrave will say 381. He is not lying. He only counts the men who die at the furnaces, not the ones who die at home afterwards.

options.text: The other workers would listen to you.
options.reply: They would. I never had a number to give them. Nobody stops working because of a feeling. 381 is different. Give me a week.

ivo.name: Doctor Ivo Marsh
ivo.greeting: Sit down if you are hurt. If you are here about a dead man, ask me. Do not open the files.

alt_greetings.text: Marsh keeps writing and does not look up.

options.text: You sign the death certificates.
options.reply: I sign what they bring me. Crushed, burned, fell, fever. 4 words and a date for a whole man.

options.text: Is the foreman's book correct?
options.reply: It is honest and it is wrong. He counts men who die at the furnaces. I also count the ones who die at home, 18 months later, coughing.

options.text: Then why do you stay?
options.reply: If I leave they will hire a doctor who counts nothing at all. That is my whole excuse and I know it is a poor one.

cadan.name: Lord Cadan Vale
cadan.greeting: You are standing on the best barley land in the kingdom and you have not looked down once.

alt_greetings.text: Vale has already decided about you and does not hide it.

options.text: How far do these farms run?
options.reply: From the river to the ridge. 4000 acres, all of it mine. There were 9 villages on this land before my father bought the rights.

options.text: What happened to the nine villages?
options.reply: They were emptied and the people were moved. The papers list all 9 by name, with the date each one was cleared. Brindle is on that list.

nessa.name: Nessa Vale
nessa.greeting: My father is busy. If you want the papers, that is my job and I am easier to find.

alt_greetings.text: Nessa keeps her hand flat on the book while she talks to you.

options.text: You keep the land papers?
options.reply: All of them. My father signs things and forgets them, then asks me what they said. I am the one who reads them.

options.text: Whose land was this before?
options.reply: 9 villages. I can name them: Brindle, Ashcote, Wenn, Upper Harrow, Lower Harrow and 4 more. I copied that list when I was 14.

pell.name: Old Pell
pell.greeting: Mind the furrow. It looks like soil. It is mostly stone, and under the stone there are old walls.

reactions.unwelcome: I answer, then I go back to my row.
reactions.welcome: You listen, so I will tell you.

alt_greetings.text: Pell keeps working his row and lets you stand there.

options.text: What was here before the farms?
options.reply: Brindle. This field was the top of the village. There was a green, a well, and a house with a broken gate. It is still Brindle to me.

options.text: Who lived in the house with the gate?
options.reply: Good people. He lent slowly and gave quickly. They had children. Nobody ever told me what became of them and I never asked.

options.text: The farmers could keep the harvest.
options.reply: They could. They have talked about it for 6 years. They needed a reason they could say out loud. 9 burned villages on paper is a reason.

ryse.name: Commander Ryse
ryse.greeting: You walk into an army camp like a man nobody has ever stopped. Enjoy it.

alt_greetings.text: Ryse does not turn round. Somebody has already described you to him.

options.text: You emptied the villages.
options.reply: I did. They gave me a list of 9 villages and one summer. I finished early. I am not sorry and I will not pretend to be.

options.text: You have trained against the king?
options.reply: For 11 years. He always attacks with the shield first and answers to the left. He learned it at 19 and nobody is allowed to beat him.

odile.name: Quartermaster Odile
odile.greeting: Supply requests on the left. Complaints anywhere you like, I do not read them.

reactions.welcome: For you, no charge this time.

alt_greetings.text: Odile shuts the book before you are close enough to read it.

options.text: Your lists of soldiers are long.
options.reply: They are as long as I am told to make them. Some of those soldiers died a month ago. The pay still leaves this tent. Ask the man who signs above me.

options.text: How does the king fight?
options.reply: Always the same way, and I will tell you for nothing. Shield first, answer to the left. I supplied the guards who trained against him for 11 years.

options.text: I know you are stealing the pay.
options.reply: Then you know what I would pay to have you stop saying it here. Name your price.

kell.name: Kell
kell.greeting: Do not do that again. Do not walk up to a man out here without making noise.

reactions.unwelcome: Stay where you are and talk.

alt_greetings.text: Kell puts a tree at his back and keeps one hand out of sight.

options.text: How long have you lived out here?
options.reply: Two winters. There is a fire and there is water and nobody orders me to carry anything. It is better than the camp was.

options.text: You were at Brindle.
options.reply: I was 19. They told us the village had fought back. It had not. It just stayed where it was and would not move. I can repeat the order word for word.

options.text: There are other deserters out here.
options.reply: 11 that I know by name. They will not come back for a pardon. They might come back for someone who already knows what we did.

options.text: I want to help the wood.
options.reply: The wood keeps no roll. You help, or you do not. We will know which.

til.name: Harbourmaster Til
til.greeting: The tide left an hour ago. Anything else, say it quietly and say it once.

reactions.unwelcome: Not here, and keep your voice down.
reactions.welcome: I will say it once, so listen.

alt_greetings.text: Til finds something at the far end of the quay that needs him.

options.text: Do many ships come through?
options.reply: Fewer than before. More than the harbour book says. Saltmarch is off the main road, so nobody comes to check.

options.text: What leaves here, and on whose orders?
options.reply: Steel, grain and money. Every month, west by sea. The king orders it and nobody signs for it. I was told to lose the cargo lists. I lost copies.

options.text: A cargo could go the wrong way.
options.reply: It has, twice. Both times we called it bad weather. I can arrange bad weather. It costs the king a month.

mira.name: Mira Sand
mira.greeting: Sit down or do not. If you came to tell me the law is the law, I have heard it.

reactions.unwelcome: I answer, but I will not defend you.
reactions.welcome: Sit down, you get all of it.

alt_greetings.text: Mira closes the file she was reading and waits for you to go.

options.text: What is it you do?
options.reply: I defend people in court who cannot pay for a lawyer. The law here decides your punishment by how much money you have.

options.text: Show me what the law does.
options.reply: 3 men broke the same wall on the same night. The rich one paid 11 shillings. The tradesman went to prison for 4 months. The poor one got 7 years.

corvin.name: Corvin Ash
corvin.greeting: You look like a man who wants something explained. That is what a bank is for. It is not free.

alt_greetings.text: Ash sends a clerk to tell you the bank is closed to you.

options.text: What does this bank do?
options.reply: It lends money to the king. The king builds with it. Everyone is happy until a payment is late.

options.text: How much does the king owe?
options.reply: Almost everything he has built, and almost all of it is owed to me. He did not pay for the ironworks with his money. He paid with mine.

peyre.name: Archivist Peyre
peyre.greeting: Quietly, please. 40 years in this room and I have got used to the quiet.

alt_greetings.text: Peyre goes back to his shelves and does not offer you a chair.

options.text: What is kept here?
options.reply: Every paper the crown ever signed. Land papers, debts, court sentences, army orders. People think an archive hides things. It does the opposite.

options.text: The land papers for the Wide Acres farms.
options.reply: Shelf 11, second copy. The 9 villages are listed by name, because the surveyor was paid for each name he wrote.

options.text: And what the crown owes.
options.reply: Shelf 11 as well. Almost all of it is owed to one man, Corvin Ash at the bank. Nobody has read the total out loud here in 6 years.

options.text: Does the church file accounts here?
options.reply: Every year, checked. Theirs always balance. They have balanced for 9 years, which is either very good work or something worse.

anselm.name: Brother Anselm
anselm.greeting: The steward is not seeing anyone. I say that 11 times a day and it is true about 10 of them.

alt_greetings.text: Anselm says the steward is not seeing anyone and does not soften it.

options.text: Who decides who she sees?
options.reply: She does. Hesper decides who is allowed into the castle at Blackcairn. There is nobody above her to ask instead.

options.text: You keep the church accounts.
options.reply: Somebody has to, or nobody can check them. They show what Hesper has taken from people over 9 years, and who paid her.

options.text: What is written on a castle pass?
options.reply: A name, a trade, a quantity of goods, and her mark next to it. I write the first three. The mark is the only part that matters.

hesper.name: Hesper
hesper.greeting: I have four minutes and you were not announced. Let us see which of us is wasting them.

alt_greetings.text: Hesper does not look up from the list she is marking.

options.text: How does a stranger get into the castle?
options.reply: With a supply pass. A name, a trade, my mark next to it, and a face the gate guards can match. That is the whole thing.

options.text: What would make you sign one?
options.reply: Something I want, or something I am afraid of. Neither is often in the room.

aurel.name: Lord Aurel Greyhold
aurel.greeting: They tell me you have been asking about the wealth levels. Ask me instead.

alt_greetings.text: Greyhold decides this is not the morning for it.

options.text: You enforce the wealth levels.
options.reply: I sign every prison sentence over 4 months in this region. I have done it for 40 years. I stopped believing in the law a long time ago.

options.text: Then stop signing them.
options.reply: Nobody has ever asked me to. I have a family, a house, and 40 years of signatures behind me. But I will not sign the next one.

arthur.name: Arthur
arthur.greeting: You came all this way and you have not drawn a weapon. Say what you came to say.

alt_greetings.text: Arthur looks at you for a long moment and decides to listen anyway.

options.text: Why did you burn the villages?
options.reply: I burned nothing. I signed an order to empty 9 villages. The soldiers did the rest. That is not an excuse. It is what happened.

options.text: Why did you need the land?
options.reply: For the ironworks. A farmer with 4 acres dies young and buries half his children. Factories are the only thing that has ever changed that.

options.text: You could have stopped.
options.reply: I could. Then the children who are not born yet would pay for it instead. I asked the villages to move. They said no. I did it anyway.

options.text: My village was one of the nine.
options.reply: I know. I do not know which one. Here is the part you will hate. They were happy. They were poor. They died at 40. All three are true.

options.text: That is not an answer.
options.reply: No. It is a trade. You can decide the first part mattered more. I decided it did not. One of us is wrong and neither of us can prove it.

options.text: You kept records of all of it.
options.reply: Every page. The dead at the ironworks, the land papers with the village names, the orders I signed. I have destroyed nothing.

dray.name: Captain Dray
dray.greeting: Stop there. You are close enough for talking.

alt_greetings.text: Dray moves between you and the gate without hurrying.

options.text: How many guards are here?
options.reply: As many as the army camp sends me. Fewer every month. This gate is built for 40 men.

options.text: Would they follow you against the king?
options.reply: No. Be glad about that. I have seen a country where the guards decided. It was worse afterwards.

_strangers_note: Generic types, not cast. §6's roster is twenty-five named people and these are not among them: a stranger has a trade, a line set shared by everyone of that trade, and no name. They exist so the world can react to you through somebody who has never met you, which is the whole point of a rumour arriving before you do. Placements are instances; the lines belong to the type.

trader.name: A trader
trader.greeting: Cloth, salt, lamp oil. Coin first, and no, I don't do favours.

alt_greetings.text: No. Whatever it is, no. I've heard about you and I'd rather keep what I've got.

options.text: What will you sell me?
options.reply: Whatever you can pay for. Sit a while, I'll find something you need.

options.text: You've never seen me before.
options.reply: Word came up the road ahead of you, and it was specific.

options.text: Busy town?
options.reply: Busy enough. The counting house keeps the hours and the rest of us keep to them.

guard.name: A bridge guard
guard.greeting: Road's open. Keep it that way and we'll not have a conversation.

alt_greetings.text: You again. Cross, and keep your hands where I can see them.

options.text: Who pays you to stand here?
options.reply: The crown pays for the bridge. The bridge pays for the post. Ask again in a month about either.

options.text: Is there another way over?
options.reply: A ford downstream. Shallow in a dry week, and nobody counts who crosses. That was not said.

options.text: Much traffic lately?
options.reply: Soldiers, going the wrong way. That is all that will be said about soldiers.

watchman.name: A watchman
watchman.greeting: Works property. Look all you like, touch nothing, and we stay friends.

alt_greetings.text: I know you. Stand where I can see you and keep your hands out.

options.text: Long shift?
options.reply: Long enough. The job is to stand here and notice things, and lately there has been a great deal to notice.

options.text: Who told you to watch this?
options.reply: Somebody who signs for it. That is as far up as anyone here has been told.

_dispositions_note: How anybody opens a conversation when they have an opinion of you, used when that person has not been written a line of their own for that band. Narration rather than speech, deliberately: a shared line in nobody's voice sounds flat coming out of a named character, but a shared line about a stance works for everyone. %s is the speaker's name. This is what makes reaction the default rather than something each line has to opt into, before it existed, four of the five named cast chatted normally to a player the whole town had turned on.

dispositions.hated: %s turns away before you can get a word out.
dispositions.wary: %s watches you a moment longer than is comfortable, and waits.
dispositions.welcome: %s is glad to see you, and does not trouble to hide it.

_reactions_note: One line per person per band, NOT per question, so it has to work in front of every answer that person has. Halgrave first read 'Vous aurez le chiffre quand meme', which fits 'how many men has it killed' and not 'what do you make here'. Check a new one against all of that character's replies before keeping it. What somebody says in front of an answer, given how they regard you. The spoken half of dispositions, which are narrated and belong to the greeting. Shown once per conversation, on the first thing they tell you, because a man who says 'you pay first' four times in one exchange is a machine with a stuck key. The rule: it says what they will or will not GIVE you, never what they think of you. A neutral standing gets nothing and the line is exactly what it has always been, so nothing regresses. 'hated' is absent on purpose: at that standing there is no conversation at all.

reactions.unwelcome: I will answer you, then you go.
reactions.welcome: For you, I can say it.
